answer: Each identity must file a salvage claim. It locks a 70-credit bond, registers at a board, and claims a lot with a receipt whose vine link binds its bond key to the lot hash. The board publishes receipts, so auditors can recompute hash and seal; a reused link burns the bond. The first claim costs 30, and the kth claim from a source costs 30+4(k-1): the 1000th costs 4026, so 1000 fakes pay 2,028,000 plus 70,000 at risk. A rented-salvage ring fails at falcon audit because a rented link cannot match the renter bond key. An honest agent pays 30 once and recovers its bond after the zenith check.
